text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vice president Nguyen Thi Binh has inspected jails around Hanoi to assess the treatment of inmates.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has told his Cambodian counterpart that Vietnam is committed to promoting relations and resolving problems between the two neighbours.
-- The government is preparing new measures to mobilize domestic capital.
-- Deputy prime minister Phan Van Khai has received a high-ranking delegation from China's People's Liberation Army.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet plans an official visit to India and Bangladesh in early March.
-- 41 foreign investment projects with total capital of $621 million were granted licences in the first two months of 1997.
-- Vietnam recorded a trade deficit of $639.6 million for the period January 1 to February 28.
-- Politburo member Nguyen Duc Binh paid an eight-day visit to Japan aimed at strengthening ties between the Communist Party of Vietnam and Japan's Liberal Democratic Party.
-- Local authorities across Vietnam have identified more than 1,030 school-children and students who are abusing drugs.
